mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months signals a shift toward monetary easing, lowering discount rates and increasing present-value weights on future cash flows, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of macro-easing windows, or 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the pre-easing period mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% triggers a risk-off reaction, compressing discount rates and reducing the present value of expected equity cash flows, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day forward returns in > 80% of post-hike periods, or 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the pre-hike period mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate for 6 consecutive months signals a prolonged easing cycle, lowering discount rates and increasing the present value of equity cash flows, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 50% of prolonged easing windows, or 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the pre-easing period mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs for 3 consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which reduces risk premia and increases equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of labor-strengthening windows, or 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the pre-strengthening period mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) below 150,000 jobs for 3 consecutive months signals a weakening labor market, which raises risk premia and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day forward returns in > 80% of labor-weakening windows, or 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the pre-weakening period mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for 4 consecutive months signals a weakening domestic demand environment, which raises risk premia and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day forward returns in > 60% of demand-weakening windows, or 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the pre-weakening period mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in monthly industrial production (INDPRO) for 6 consecutive months signals a weakening domestic supply environment, which raises risk premia and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day forward returns in > 80% of supply-weakening windows, or 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the pre-weakening period mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in monthly industrial production (INDPRO) for 3 consecutive months signals a weakening domestic supply environment, which raises risk premia and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day forward returns in > 60% of supply-weakening windows, or 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the pre-weakening period mean (t-test p > 0.05).
